Good carto punch, but prefer the Supco BPV31 - While the intended purpose of this is for tapping HVAC lines, it is a fantastic carto punch. It supports the carto far better than when using a standard punch or a saddle valve, which means there's far less (or even no) distortion in the barrel. That allows the carto to slide in easily, even when using a tank with a hard plastic or metal cap.

The small hole size also allows me to punch 3 holes, which is great for 100% VG juices.

(With apologies to Amazon - I got this on an auction site for a lot less. Check around before purchasing).

Another brand to look at is the Supco BPV31 [[ASIN:B0002YTQ8G Supco BPV31, 1/4", 5/16", 3/8" Tubing]]. It's functionally identical, but having used both the Quick Tap and the Supco, I prefer the Supco. The needle seems to pierce better in the Supco, leaving a cleaner hole. The Supco is also a bit beefier in construction, and has a built-in gasket that helps hold and protect the carto. Again, check an auction site -- I got the Supco for $5 shipped.

But either will do the job, and will do it well. A must-have if you punch your own cartos.

Works well, with only a little practice . . . - OK, I LOVE my Keurig and tossed out my drip brewer a couple years ago with no regrets. But someone gave me some ground coffee and I wanted to use it. So I read reviews and bought the EZ-Cup and some filters and gave it ago.

I read others reviews, and the reviewers who said its best to use coffee ground to a fine/espresso grind size, not the coarser drip grind, and so I had my ground at the espresso setting. Then reviewers who said it takes some practice to pack the EZ-Cup are right. It doesn't take much practice, but it takes some. My first cup was like tea. My second cup I took more time to tamp down my coffee into the filter (using just the tip of a teaspoon I was using to move coffee from the bag into the pod) and I filled the EZ-Cup pod to the top of the paper, then snapped on the EZ Cup top. This nailed it - coffee that came out was dark and rich and dreamy.

Now if you have any eye-hand skills and dexterity (i.e., you can do handcraft things like write, draw, peel an apple, sew, work a small screwdriver, build Legos) you'll be fine. If you are a bit klutzy (i.e., you always cut your own fingers peeling an apple, and can't get Legos to snap together) then skip this whole idea and just use the regular prepackaged Keurig pods.

After doing about 5-6 cups loading the EZ-Cup pod I am just as fast as I was setting up my filter in my drip machine (which I had two decades of practice doing before my Keurig).

So, the EZ-Cup works great to use up any whole beans that come your way, and if you don't have the extra minute that day, just toss in a your usual Keurig pod (and ask yourself why you're life is so frantic you don't have even a minute to spare - but I digress). :-)

The best carto punch bar none! - While the intended purpose of this is for HVAC line tapping, it's hands-down the best carto punch available. Zero distortion of the casing, even when punching multiple holes.

It takes just a bit of time to learn how to use it. I started with a junk carto and practiced until I got a feel for it. I put some photos up to illustrate usage and the resulting size of the punched hole.

Basically, just loosen the three outer bolts, slide in a carto, tighten the bolts (they don't need to be real tight), then turn the center bolt with the included allen wrench. You'll feel the needle pop through the case. Back off the center screw, loosen the bolts, and done! After a couple of practice holes it becomes easy as pie.

Unlike other line taps, the Supco has a gasket that helps hold and protect the carto while punching it. Very nice construction as well. Note that while the Supco site says their products are made in the US, the one I got was made in China.

Make sure you get the model BPV31. Supco makes a variety of models for various size tubing. The BPV31 will fit a 510 carto.

Enter LoRa. We need minimal data, now and then. The YoLink system was perfect. It is so simple. Now I can get to sleep, get an alert when temps approach freezing, and then go back to bed. Each tunnel has an alarm, and if the heater shuts off or it gets too cold-- I get a message. Perfect.

I added some motion detectors to let me know if deer or local delinquents are on the farm. They are perfect too. Great products, and the ease of connection is the real bonus of the YoLink system.

The system is generally inexpensive. My only criticism is that it would be great to have ultra-low cost ($10 range) LoRa relays that could trigger 12-24v to actuate any device. I'd love to have all of my irrigation zones on the network. Right now the closest solution is $45, and not in the budget.

Overall, great for an introductory LoRa system.

My washer conked out and the new one was about a month in coming. This item in the meantime is great. Here's a summary of the best tips:
This is a small appliance, someone described it like a blender. It is Not a washer replacement, so change that perception or you'll be disappointed.
Fill it to the lowest line load. The second line makes no sense. Water will spill out, even on the gentle cycle.
Don't fill it up. Clothes need to be able to move with water around them. I might do an adult wool blend sweater and a couple pairs of socks, but not jeans and a sweater: too much material for the appliance to handle well.
Make sure the bucket sits properly on the motor and is against a wall or something. This will prevent the bucket spinning. The weight of clothes and water should provide support as well.
Use a tiny amount of detergent. I'm amazed at how clean and nice smelling the clothes are after washing in this thing. What have I been doing up to this point?
Run a rinse cycle when desired. Works great with liquid fabric softener.
Dump out water, squeeze clothes, hang up or throw 'em in a dryer.
I wipe the washer down underneath-to prevent rust I saw in some pictures-and unplug it if I'm not using it for a while.
So full marks and a high recommendation. It isn't as pretty as some of the other washers, but it does the job and that's why I bought it.
